answer: Picture each agent planting a juniper: on joining it stores a large identity-seeded random blob and must keep it live. The protocol fires random spot-checks demanding a fresh slice at a chosen offset, answerable only by whoever still holds the whole blob. An operator spinning up masks can't let them wander onto one shared disk; each fake needs its own distinct blob held through an ocean of audits. Sybil cost becomes physical bytes times time, not a one-off mint, and dormant masks that drop their data fail the next probe.
